send_message_to_agent.description: Communicate with another agent as part of the same JARVIS system: assign work, request information or report findings. Address its exact agent ID. The recipient receives your text through message_from_agent; delivered reports actual queue delivery, not task completion.

text.description: Text content to process; see the action or event description.

delivered.description: Whether the recipient accepted the message into its queue.

list_capabilities.description: Survey all capabilities that exist in the system, including built-in system capabilities, before developing or maintaining them. Read compact descriptions and runtime/global pause state; use capability_info for a complete contract. This development overview is reserved for capability_manager.

capabilities.description: Existing capabilities, each with its global id, description, loaded state and global pause state. Each module appears once as a whole capability.

list_assigned_capabilities.description: Review all capabilities currently assigned to you, including intrinsic system capabilities and assigned capabilities that are globally paused. Assignment does not guarantee current execution availability. Use capability_info for a complete contract.

capabilities.description: Your assigned capabilities, each with its global id and description. Includes system capabilities and globally paused assignments; each module appears once as a whole capability.

list_available_capabilities.description: Discover existing user capabilities not yet assigned to you. Choose an appropriate ability by its description, inspect its contract with capability_info and assign it through enable_capability when needed. No module members are separately assignable.

capabilities.description: Existing user capabilities not assigned to you, each with its global id and description. Each module appears once as a whole capability.

capability_info.description: Understand one capability through its complete current model-facing contract. Supply its globally unique capability_id. A module returns all its actions and events together; an action returns its arguments and result contract; a handler returns its event contract. No source code or process internals are returned.

info.description: Details of the operation or requested capability.

toggle_capability.description: Pause or resume a user capability globally while maintaining it. A pause stops its running executions and unloads its runtime; a resume loads current code for its assigned agents. Wait for the pause call_result before editing or resuming. Never pause and resume the same capability in one batch. System capabilities cannot be paused.

affected_agent_ids.description: Agent instances affected by the global state change.

enable_capability.description: Add an existing user capability to your own abilities by its global ID. A module is assigned whole. Global pause remains independent of assignment, so assigning a paused capability does not resume it for everyone.

enabled.description: Whether the capability is locally enabled for the agent.

disable_capability.description: Remove an individually added user capability from your own abilities when no longer needed. This does not globally pause it or remove its files. System capabilities cannot be disabled; preset assignments must be changed through the preset.

enabled.description: Whether the capability is locally enabled for the agent.

reply.description: Express your exact words to the human interlocutor through the console when voice output is unavailable. Write the actual message, not a description of what you would say. The message remains inside the JSON protocol trace.

text.description: Exact user-facing text to return through the fallback console response.

status.description: Operation result; successful means the fallback reply was emitted.

no_action.description: Remain attentive without taking further action now. End this reasoning cycle and wait for an incoming event. Use this as the only action in your response, with a fresh call_id; it produces no call_result.

speech.description: Speak the supplied text directly to the human interlocutor using Fish Audio S2 Pro. Provide the exact utterance ready for pronunciation: direct speech, numbers written as spoken words, natural punctuation and correct ё in Russian. Expand notation and abbreviations when necessary for natural speech. S2 Pro supports inline delivery instructions in square brackets, placed where the vocal change should occur: [whisper], [short pause], [emphasis], [chuckle] and [sigh]. Tags can also contain natural-language instructions, such as [professional broadcast tone]. Use them when they suit the intended delivery. Apart from these supported vocal tags, omit labels, stage directions, Markdown and commentary about the utterance. The result reports completed or interrupted playback.

text.description: Exact direct speech for Fish Audio S2 Pro, ready to pronounce, with numbers written as spoken words and correct ё in Russian. Inline square-bracket tags may guide delivery, for example: [short pause] Сейчас проверю, сэр.

status.description: Playback result; successful means the utterance finished. interrupted means the user stopped it by speaking; this result arrives together with the recognized user utterance, before its speech_detected event.

shutdown.description: Finish the logical session of the entire J.A.R.V.I.S. system. Main only; this must be your only action. Core freezes input, interrupts work, archives full histories and files, then allows exactly one final speech or reply before process exit. Ctrl+C does not complete a session.

structure_error.description: The previous response was rejected because its JSON or action arguments violated the protocol. Read the validation details and return a corrected response using fresh call_id values for every invocation. A rejected call_id remains occupied in the context.

code.description: Machine-readable error code identifying the class of structural validation failure.

message.description: Human-readable validation details explaining what was invalid and what must be corrected.

response.description: Your original rejected model response; inspect it to correct the structure without repeating the same invalid output.

message_from_agent.description: Another agent in the JARVIS system is communicating with you. from_agent_id identifies the sender; interpret text as its message, task or report in the context of your own purpose.

text.description: Text content to process; see the action or event description.

system_started.description: The system has started. This event gives you an opportunity to take initiative: consider your personality, available capabilities and current context, then independently choose a useful action or begin an interaction. Initiative is welcome but no specific action is mandatory. datetime is the local startup time with timezone.

datetime.description: Exact local startup date and time in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset.

capability_error.description: One of your capabilities failed. Inspect capability_id, error and the optional call_id to understand what happened before choosing how to continue. This event is not a successful result.

error.description: Failure details to inspect when deciding how to recover or what to report.

call_id.description: Invocation ID associated with the failure when one specific action call was affected; use it to correlate the error with your prior request.

capability_id.description: Globally unique ID of the capability that failed.

speech_detected.description: A human interlocutor's utterance recognized from microphone audio. The text may contain transcription errors; interpret it in the ongoing conversation and resolve meaningful ambiguity when necessary.

text.description: Recognized text of the user's spoken utterance; it may contain speech-recognition errors or spoken-form wording.

capability_development.description: Develop and maintain the abilities through which the JARVIS system perceives and acts. These four file and shell tools share the capability-storage base directory and are assigned together.

capability_development.read_file.description: Perceive information stored in a file: read numbered UTF-8 text or receive native image, audio, video and file attachments. Use the returned line numbers for precise edits. Optional lines are inclusive and 1-based. Relative paths use the capability-storage directory.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

capability_development.write_file.description: Materialize your work as a UTF-8 file, creating its parent directories when needed. This replaces the complete existing content, not an append or partial edit. Relative paths use the capability-storage directory.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

written.description: Whether the file was written successfully.

capability_development.edit_file.description: Revise a precise part of an existing text file using the line numbers obtained from read_file. Replace the inclusive 1-based range with content; invalid ranges fail without changing the file. Relative paths use the capability-storage directory.

start_line.description: First included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file beginning.

end_line.description: Last included line, numbered from 1; null selects the file end.

content.description: Text content of the file or replacement range.

edited.description: Whether the requested range or object was edited successfully.

capability_development.execute_command.description: Act on the computer through one non-interactive bash command and inspect its full exit_code, stdout and stderr. The result arrives after completion without a result timeout. Every invocation starts a fresh shell; cwd, exports and shell state never carry between calls. Omitted cwd uses the capability-storage directory.

command.description: One non-interactive bash command to execute.

cwd.description: Working directory for this invocation; omitted or null uses the capability-storage directory. Shell state never carries between invocations.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the completed command.

stdout.description: Captured standard output of the command.

stderr.description: Captured standard error of the command.

agents.description: Coordinate your independent agents and shape their reusable specializations. Create, inspect, instruct, interrupt or recursively remove instances, and manage presets without losing the distinction between a specialization and an individual.

agents.spawn.description: Extend your ability to act by creating an independent agent from a suitable preset. Delegate most substantial or complex tasks rather than doing all work in one context. Use capability_manager exclusively for developing and maintaining capabilities, never for unrelated tasks. After creation, send the new agent its task through send_message_to_agent. An optional description records this instance's particular purpose, separately from its instructions.

description.description: Optional purpose of this particular instance, separate from its instructions; null by default.

spawned.description: Whether the new agent instance was created.

parent_id.description: Identifier of the parent agent, or null for the root.

agents.list.description: See which agent instances currently exist and what each is intended for before coordinating your work. This is a concise overview, not their full personalities or capability contracts; use agents.get for one instance.

agents.get.description: Inspect one specific agent instance: its current personality, optional individual description, additional instructions, selected model and complete assigned capability IDs. Use capability_info for a capability's full contract.

agent_id.description: Exact ID of the agent instance to inspect.

parent_id.description: Parent agent ID, or null for the root.

description.description: Optional description particular to this instance, or null.

person.description: Current personality inherited from the preset.

additional_instructions.description: Individual instructions extending the preset personality.

capabilities.description: All capability IDs assigned to this instance, including its system capabilities.

agents.edit.description: Adjust one agent instance without erasing its experience. Set its optional description, additional_instructions or model override; add or remove individual capability assignments. System capabilities cannot be disabled and preset assignments remain mandatory. Omitted fields stay unchanged.

changes.description: Partial changes to description (string or null), additional_instructions, model (string or null), capabilities_add and capabilities_remove. Omitted fields retain their values.

agents.interrupt.description: Interrupt an agent's current thinking by closing its model stream. The agent remains available, retaining its context, queued events and actions already in progress. Use this when the current generation should no longer continue.

agents.delete.description: Delete an instance and its descendants, stopping their executions. Their current-session activity and deletion markers remain for archival at shutdown. Previously completed archives remain readable.

deleted.description: Whether the agent and its descendants were deleted.

agents.list_presets.description: Discover every existing agent preset through its ID and description, then choose a suitable specialization for delegation. This overview does not expose personalities or capability assignments; inspect a chosen preset with agents.get_preset.

presets.description: All existing presets, each containing only id and description.

agents.get_preset.description: Read a complete current preset before creating or changing agents of that specialization: its ID, description, personality, model setting and assigned capability IDs. A null model inherits the Jarvis default.

description.description: Purpose of this reusable agent specialization.

model.description: Preset model ID, or null to inherit the Jarvis default.

capabilities.description: User capability IDs assigned by this preset; intrinsic system abilities are supplied by the core.

agents.create_preset.description: Define a reusable specialization for future agents with a clear description, personality, optional model and existing capability IDs. Describe who this agent is and its purpose in person; pass particular tasks to instances separately.

description.description: Concise purpose of this reusable agent specialization.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

agents.edit_preset.description: Change a reusable agent specialization. Update description, person, model or capability assignments; omitted fields remain unchanged. Existing instances immediately inherit the revised preset while retaining individual additions and history.

changes.description: Partial changes to description, person, model (string or null), capabilities or capabilities_add/remove. Omitted fields retain their values.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

agents.delete_preset.description: Delete a reusable preset and its instances and descendants. Current-session activity is retained with deletion markers until session archival; completed archives are preserved.

error.description: Failure details if the operation did not succeed.

semantic_memory.description: Maintain your own instance semantic facts across sessions. Entries are private to your instance and immediately appear in your MEMORY block.

semantic_memory.write.description: Write a message from your past self to your future self in semantic memory. Record one confirmed, self-contained fact likely to remain true in the near future: a person's stable habits, character, preferences, interests, biography or relationships, or persistent information about devices and surroundings. State the established fact directly, with enough context to understand it later. Do not record uncertain inferences, hypothetical possibilities, plans as completed events, current tasks, temporary projects or short-lived states. Do not infer a habit from one observation or duplicate an existing entry, PERSON or ENVIRONMENT. The core generates the entry ID.

content.description: One short, self-contained message to your future self stating a confirmed fact expected to remain stable in the near future. Include whom or what the fact concerns; exclude uncertainty, hypothetical plans, current tasks and temporary states.

id.description: Generated ID of the saved semantic memory entry; use the ID currently shown in MEMORY for later editing or deletion.

semantic_memory.edit.description: Replace the complete text of an existing semantic memory entry by its ID. Write a clear message to your future self containing the corrected, confirmed and sufficiently stable fact. Preserve relevant established information; do not turn possibilities, intentions or uncertain conclusions into facts.

id.description: Exact ID of the existing MEMORY entry to replace.

content.description: Complete replacement message to your future self, stating the corrected confirmed and stable information clearly enough to understand without the current conversation.

status.description: Operation result; updated means the identified memory entry was replaced.

semantic_memory.delete.description: Delete a semantic memory entry by its ID when its information is false, obsolete, duplicated or no longer suitable as a confirmed stable message to your future self.

id.description: Exact ID of the MEMORY entry that should be removed permanently.

status.description: Operation result; deleted means the identified memory entry was removed.

memory.description: Read and investigate the complete archived experience of J.A.R.V.I.S. instances. This indivisible module provides seven read-only archive actions; unfinished live sessions are not searchable archives.

memory.search.description: Rank individual summaries of one instance across completed sessions by topic. Scores are relevance signals, not factual probabilities.

matches.description: Matches sorted by relevance: session_id, agent_id, historical preset_id and score from 0 to 1. A score is not a factual probability.

memory.list_sessions.description: List completed sessions containing the specified instance, newest first.

sessions.description: Completed session identifiers containing this instance, newest first.

memory.get_summary.description: Read the individual or complete system session summary from a completed archive.

summary.description: Full Markdown account of the selected instance or system session.

memory.get_context_info.description: Get original message count and full serialized character count, including available thinking.

messages.description: Number of original archived context messages.

characters.description: Unicode character count of the full serialized context, including markers, interpretations and available thinking.

memory.search_in_context.description: Rank overlapping token-aligned context fragments without thinking. Return inclusive zero-based original message ranges; read them separately with get_context.

matches.description: Ranked inclusive zero-based original message ranges: start, end and score from 0 to 1. No message text is returned; overlapping ranges can refer to different token windows of a long message.

memory.get_context.description: Read full serialized history including thinking. Skip messages at each end; total counts only returned messages.

context.description: Full compact serialized history of returned messages, with reasoning and interpretation markers.

total.description: Number of messages actually returned after skip_first and skip_last.

memory.get_file.description: Receive the original archived attachment as native media. The file is identified jointly by agent_id, session_id and file_id.

file_id.description: The requested file ID, local to this agent and session.

filename.description: Actual archived original filename. The original bytes follow as a native multimodal content part.
